hints.title: Two Row Patterns
hints.text: A row of 3 cells with 3 colors can only take two pattern types: two colors used or three colors used.

hints.title: Base Counts for n = 1
hints.text: For the first row, there are 3 * 2 * 1 = 6 ways with three colors, and 3 * 2 * 1 = 6 ways with two colors.

hints.title: Pattern Transitions
hints.text: A two-color row transitions to 3 two-color and 2 three-color rows. A three-color row transitions to 2 two-color and 2 three-color rows. Apply modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def numOfWays(self, n: int) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        aba = 6
        abc = 6
        for _ in range(2, n + 1):
            new_aba = (3 * aba + 2 * abc) % MOD
            new_abc = (2 * aba + 2 * abc) % MOD
            aba, abc = new_aba, new_abc
        return (aba + abc) % MOD
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 3^(3N) possible colorings is astronomically large for n up to 5000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Group equivalence reduces states to just two types (ABA and ABC) using O(1) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate deduces the recurrence: aba_next = 3 * aba + 2 * abc, abc_next = 2 * aba + 2 * abc.
